items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: It’s a Dr. Lonnie Smith song

ctx.x: I just, you know I just have a different approach because what would I do now, for me, is a positive thought, not a negative thought. Because if he played something and he left me to a point, say a challenge, what do I have to add? How can I add to the music after everything that he already gave? So for me it’s not like oh my God he played so beautiful now I’m going to — I mean there’s no time and no room for negative thoughts at this point, it’s only about think about the music and you have to really be —…

definitely somebody I admire so much and it was such a thrill to have him, it was the D.C. Jazz Festival and actually he recorded that tune with me on my album Ciaroscuro, that “And the World Weeps.” It’s a Dr. Lonnie Smith song, a very simple minor eight bars, the song is just powerful and simple like many songs. And it’s just great because it can really show how for me how to be connected with your soul and how the clarinet can be so expressive and get such a wide range of emotions. And Pacquito is such an…

You’ve done very well in the polls, DownBeat, in the last few years, and I wonder if people who are voting for you, if it’s more than the way — how am I — I’m trying to say that people will like what you do not just because of the way you play your instrument, it’s the music you choose to play, at least this is my attitude. Do you think part of your success in those pollings have to do with what you’ve done with combining music and the variety of things you present?
